q: What is a class in StudyLamb, and what can it hold?
a: A class is one school subject, like Science or Math. It has a name and a color, and it can hold as many exams as you like.

q: Name three kinds of files you can upload as study materials.
a: Any three of: PDF, photo, Word document (.docx), plain text file, or pasted text. Files can be up to 25 megabytes.

q: What does the syllabus upload do?
a: It reads your syllabus and creates your classes and their major exams for you, including dates when they are listed.

q: If your notes contradict the textbook chapter, what goes into the study guide?
a: Only the version that matches the chapter material. Chapter material is the source of truth, and contradicting claims are left out.

q: Why might a fact show up more often in your cards?
a: Because it appeared in many of your notes. Repeated information is treated as important and gets more weight.

q: What does StudyLamb do when you upload a file identical to one it already processed?
a: It skips the duplicate instead of processing it again, saving time and BrainBucks.

q: How do you build a final review at the end of the semester?
a: Tap Final review: pick classes on the classes page, check the classes on your final, and tap Build final review. It combines all their cards and questions into one exam, free.

q: How do you rename a chapter?
a: On the exam Home page, find the chapter in the Chapters card and tap the pencil next to its name.

q: What do blue, red, and green screens mean in StudyLamb?
a: Blue is for learning, red is for quizzing and recall, and green marks a correct answer.

q: What does StudyLamb say instead of Wrong when you miss an answer?
a: Not yet, plus what to try next. It praises strategy and effort rather than the person.

q: Explain how spaced repetition chooses which flashcards you see.
a: Cards you know well return later as quick review, while cards you struggle with come back sooner and more often. It works on every page.

q: What do you see while flashcard audio reads a card?
a: A highlighted word and bouncy ball help you follow Professor Lamby's voice. Word timing is approximate.

q: Why is drawing on cards still readable?
a: The drawing ink is slightly transparent, so the card's words show through clearly.

q: Describe the Memorize game and its passing rule.
a: You see the first letter of each word and type the words, across three rounds. You pass a round with accuracy strictly above ninety percent, and a neighboring keyboard key counts as a match.

q: What feedback do you get the moment you type a wrong letter in Memorize?
a: The word turns red right away, you see the key you pressed, and the correct word is shown so you can keep going.

q: What is the difference between Q and A mode and Abstract mode on the Listen tab?
a: Q and A reads every question and answer in order. Abstract turns the topic into a fun, memorable audio lesson with stories and memory tricks.

q: Where do your uploaded originals and personal notes live?
a: On the exam Home page: What you uploaded shows your files word for word, and My notes holds your typed or spoken notes.

q: How do you add a photo of a notebook page to your notes?
a: Tap the Camera button on Home; it opens your camera directly, and the page is read in and folded into the study set.

q: What does the daily goal chip like eight of twenty mean?
a: You have done eight of your twenty planned reviews today. It is a small visible win, not a streak.

q: How do you start a sample exam, and what choices do you get?
a: Open Sample exam, optionally pick a chapter, choose five, ten, twenty, or all questions, and tap Start exam.

q: What does the retake button do after a sample exam?
a: It starts a new round with only the questions you marked Not yet, so you practice exactly what needs work.

q: What happens to questions you miss on a sample exam?
a: They come back more often in Cards and Practice until you know them.

q: How does StudyLamb plan studying when your exam is two days away versus three weeks away?
a: Two days away triggers cram mode: unknown cards first, more in less time. Three weeks away spreads new cards into small daily sets with lots of review as you go.

q: What kinds of due dates can you set?
a: Test, Exam, or Homework, each with a date, set in the When is it due box on the exam Home page.

q: Give two examples of actions that cost BrainBucks and one that is free.
a: Costs: building a study set (five plus one per PDF or photo), making an episode (three), a new read-aloud clip or spoken note (one). Free: replaying audio that was already made.

q: What warnings protect your BrainBucks balance?
a: A low balance of five or fewer pops a top up reminder, and any action costing ninety five percent or more of your balance shows a warning with cheaper options before you confirm.

q: What is the grace buffer?
a: If you run out mid task, StudyLamb lets the task go three BrainBucks into the negative to finish its current step. Beyond that it pauses until you top up.

q: Name three supports you can turn on in Settings.
a: Any three of: Dyslexia structured literacy with the Word Lab, ADHD short chunks and visible progress, read aloud, and adjustable text size and spacing. Timers stay off by default.

q: What happens to your BrainBucks when an AI task fails?
a: They are refunded automatically. Failed work is never billed.
